questions.question: What is the main function of the heart?
questions.correctAnswer: To pump blood through the body
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscular pump: each contraction pushes oxygen-rich blood out to the body and brings oxygen-poor blood back toward the lungs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The heart pumps blood.

questions.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The four chambers are two atria on top, which receive blood, and two ventricles below, which pump it out.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The heart has four chambers.

questions.question: What is the normal resting heart rate for a healthy teenager?
questions.correctAnswer: About 60 to 100 beats per minute
questions.explanation: Resting rate is measured when you are calm and still; teens tend to run a little higher than adults because their bodies are still growing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Resting heart rate is 60 to 100.

questions.question: What is blood pressure?
questions.correctAnswer: The force of blood against artery walls
distractors: The amount of blood in the body
questions.explanation: It is reported as two numbers, like 120 over 80: the pressure when the heart squeezes and the lower pressure when it relaxes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Blood pressure is force on artery walls.

questions.question: What is the main function of the lungs?
questions.correctAnswer: To exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: The lungs exchange gases with the blood.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lungs swap gases.

questions.question: How many minutes of physical activity do teens need most days?
questions.correctAnswer: At least 60 minutes
questions.explanation: The 60 minutes can be split up through the day, and any activity that raises the heart rate counts - sports, biking, brisk walking, or active play.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Teens need 60 minutes a day.

questions.question: What type of exercise strengthens the heart?
questions.correctAnswer: Aerobic exercise
questions.explanation: Aerobic exercise, like running, strengthens the heart.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Aerobic exercise helps the heart.

questions.question: What is the benefit of warming up before exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: It prepares muscles and reduces injury risk
questions.explanation: A warm-up raises muscle temperature and blood flow gradually, so muscles work and stretch without a sudden strain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Warm up first.

questions.question: What is the benefit of cooling down after exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the heart rate return to normal gradually
questions.explanation: Stopping suddenly lets blood pool in the legs; an easy cool-down keeps it moving while breathing and heart rate settle back down.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cool down slowly.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep do teenagers need each night?
questions.correctAnswer: 8 to 10 hours
questions.explanation: Sleep is when the brain locks in learning and the body releases growth hormone, which is why teens need more sleep than adults.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Teens need 8 to 10 hours.

questions.question: What is a nutrient?
questions.correctAnswer: A substance in food that the body needs to grow and stay healthy
questions.explanation: There are six nutrient groups - carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water - and each one does a different job.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nutrients feed the body.

questions.question: What are the six main nutrients?
questions.correctAnswer: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water
distractors: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, sugar, salt, and caffeine
Vitamins, minerals, water, sugar, salt, and fat
Proteins, fats, vitamins, sugar, salt, and water
questions.explanation: Sugar, salt, and caffeine are ingredients or stimulants, not nutrient groups; the real six each do work the body cannot skip.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Six nutrients keep you healthy.

questions.question: What is the main function of carbohydrates?
questions.correctAnswer: To provide quick energy
questions.explanation: The body breaks carbohydrates into glucose, its fastest fuel; fiber is the carbohydrate form that instead supports digestion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Carbs give quick energy.

questions.question: What is the main function of protein?
questions.correctAnswer: To build and repair body tissues
questions.explanation: Protein supplies amino acids, the building blocks used to grow muscle, heal cuts, and build enzymes and hormones.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Protein builds and repairs.

questions.question: What is the main function of fats?
questions.correctAnswer: To store energy and protect organs
questions.explanation: Fat is the long-term fuel tank: it stores more than twice the energy of carbohydrates per gram, insulates the body, and cushions organs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fats store energy.

questions.question: What is the main function of vitamins?
questions.correctAnswer: To help the body work properly in small amounts
questions.explanation: Vitamins provide no calories - they act as helpers that let the body's chemical reactions run correctly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Vitamins help the body work.

questions.question: Which vitamin does sunlight help the body make?
questions.correctAnswer: Vitamin D
questions.explanation: Sunlight helps skin make vitamin D.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sunlight makes vitamin D.

questions.question: Which vitamin helps prevent scurvy and is found in citrus fruit?
questions.correctAnswer: Vitamin C
questions.explanation: Without vitamin C the body cannot make collagen properly, and the bleeding gums and weakness of scurvy follow.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Citrus has vitamin C.

questions.question: What mineral is important for strong bones and teeth?
questions.correctAnswer: Calcium
questions.explanation: About 99 percent of the body's calcium sits in bones and teeth, so calcium-rich foods matter most while the skeleton is still growing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Calcium builds bones.

questions.question: What mineral helps carry oxygen in the blood?
questions.correctAnswer: Iron
questions.explanation: Iron in hemoglobin carries oxygen.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Iron carries oxygen.

questions.question: Why is water important for the body?
questions.correctAnswer: It carries nutrients, regulates temperature, and removes waste
questions.explanation: Blood is mostly water, and the body constantly loses water through sweat, breath, and urine, so it must be replaced every day.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Water does many jobs.

questions.question: How much water should a teenager drink each day?
questions.correctAnswer: About 8 cups, or as thirst and activity require
questions.explanation: Treat the 8 cups as a rough guide: thirst is a useful signal, and sports, heat, or illness all raise how much you need.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Drink about 8 cups.

questions.question: What is a balanced diet?
questions.correctAnswer: Eating a variety of foods from all food groups in the right amounts
questions.explanation: No single food contains every nutrient, so eating across grains, protein foods, dairy, fruits, and vegetables covers the gaps.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Balance means variety.

questions.question: What food group do bread, rice, and pasta belong to?
questions.correctAnswer: Grains
questions.explanation: Grains are the seeds of grasses such as wheat, rice, and oats; bread and pasta are foods made from grain flours.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bread is a grain.

questions.question: What food group do milk, cheese, and yogurt belong to?
questions.correctAnswer: Dairy
questions.explanation: Dairy foods all start as milk from animals, and they are grouped together because they are rich in calcium.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Milk is dairy.

questions.question: What is the difference between whole grains and refined grains?
questions.correctAnswer: Whole grains keep the bran and germ; refined grains remove them
questions.explanation: Milling strips away the fiber, B vitamins, and healthy oils held in the bran and germ, leaving mostly starch behind.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Whole grains keep it all.

questions.question: What is fiber?
questions.correctAnswer: Plant material that helps digestion
questions.explanation: The body cannot digest fiber, so it adds bulk that moves food through the intestines and feeds helpful gut bacteria.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fiber helps digestion.

questions.question: What is a calorie?
questions.correctAnswer: A unit of energy in food
questions.explanation: Food labels use calories to show energy content; a teen typically needs roughly 2,000 to 2,500 a day depending on activity.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Calories measure energy.

questions.question: What is the best first step if someone is choking and cannot breathe?
questions.correctAnswer: Perform abdominal thrusts (the Heimlich maneuver)
distractors: Pat their back only and wait
questions.explanation: If the person can still cough or speak, encourage coughing; abdominal thrusts are for a fully blocked airway, when they cannot breathe at all.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Heimlich helps choking.

questions.question: What should you do first for a minor cut?
questions.correctAnswer: Clean it with water and cover it with a bandage
questions.explanation: Washing dirt and germs out first lowers the risk of infection; the bandage then keeps the cut clean while it heals.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Clean and cover a cut.

questions.question: What should you do for a nosebleed?
questions.correctAnswer: Lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose
distractors: Lean back and tilt the head up
questions.explanation: Leaning forward keeps blood out of the throat, and pinching the soft part squeezes the bleeding vessels shut while a clot forms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lean forward for a nosebleed.

questions.question: What is the first step in treating a burn?
questions.correctAnswer: Cool it with cool running water
questions.explanation: Cool running water pulls heat out of the skin and limits damage; ice can freeze tissue, and butter traps heat and germs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cool a burn with water.

questions.question: What number should you call in the United States for an emergency?
questions.explanation: A 911 dispatcher sends help and can also talk you through first aid, such as CPR, while the ambulance is on its way.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Call 911 in an emergency.

questions.question: What is CPR?
questions.correctAnswer: Chest compressions and rescue breaths to keep blood flowing
questions.explanation: When the heart stops, chest compressions squeeze it by hand to keep oxygen moving until it restarts or help arrives.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: CPR keeps blood flowing.

questions.question: What is a fracture?
questions.correctAnswer: A broken bone
questions.explanation: Breaks range from hairline cracks to complete snaps; a suspected fracture should be kept still and checked with an X-ray.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fracture means broken bone.

questions.question: What is a sprain?
questions.correctAnswer: An injury to a ligament
questions.explanation: Ligaments are the tough bands that connect bone to bone; a sprain stretches or tears them, most often in the ankle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A sprain hurts a ligament.

questions.question: What does RICE stand for in first aid?
questions.correctAnswer: Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation
questions.explanation: Rest protects the injury, ice narrows blood vessels to limit swelling, compression supports the area, and elevation helps fluid drain away.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: RICE is rest, ice, compression, elevation.

questions.question: What is a vaccine?
questions.correctAnswer: A substance that helps the body build immunity to a disease
distractors: A medicine that cures all diseases
questions.explanation: Most vaccines use a weakened or inactive germ, or a piece of one, so the immune system can practice without a real infection.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Vaccines build immunity.

questions.question: What is the immune system?
questions.correctAnswer: The body's defense against germs and disease
questions.explanation: White blood cells and antibodies do the defending: they recognize germs and destroy them or mark them for removal.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The immune system defends you.

questions.question: What is a virus?
questions.correctAnswer: A tiny particle that needs a host cell to reproduce
questions.explanation: A virus is not alive on its own - it must get inside a cell and hijack the cell's machinery to make copies of itself.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Viruses need a host.

questions.question: What is a bacterium?
questions.correctAnswer: A single-celled organism that can live on its own
questions.explanation: Unlike viruses, bacteria are complete living cells; many are harmless or even helpful, and only some cause disease.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bacteria are single cells.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent the spread of germs?
questions.correctAnswer: Wash hands often with soap and water
questions.explanation: Soap and water lift germs off the skin and rinse them away - the single most effective everyday germ defense.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wash your hands.

questions.question: How long should you wash your hands?
questions.correctAnswer: At least 20 seconds
questions.explanation: Twenty seconds of scrubbing with soap, about the time it takes to hum 'Happy Birthday' twice, covers all hand surfaces.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wash for 20 seconds.

questions.question: What is a communicable disease?
questions.correctAnswer: A disease that can spread from person to person
questions.explanation: Colds, flu, and COVID-19 are communicable: they pass between people through droplets, touch, or shared air.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Communicable means it spreads.

questions.question: What is a noncommunicable disease?
questions.correctAnswer: A disease that cannot spread from person to person, such as diabetes
questions.explanation: Diabetes and asthma develop from genes, body processes, and environment - you cannot catch them from a classmate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Noncommunicable does not spread.

questions.question: What is diabetes?
questions.correctAnswer: A condition where the body cannot control blood sugar properly
questions.explanation: In diabetes the body makes too little insulin or cannot use it well, so sugar builds up in the blood instead of entering cells.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Diabetes affects blood sugar.

questions.question: What is asthma?
questions.correctAnswer: A condition where airways narrow and make breathing hard
questions.explanation: During an asthma flare the airway muscles tighten and the lining swells, so air must move through a much narrower tube.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Asthma makes breathing hard.

questions.question: What is an allergy?
questions.correctAnswer: An immune reaction to a harmless substance
questions.explanation: The immune system mistakes a harmless substance, such as pollen or peanuts, for a threat and overreacts to it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Allergies are immune reactions.

questions.question: What is stress?
questions.correctAnswer: The body's response to a challenge or demand
questions.explanation: Short-term stress sharpens focus and energy, but stress that never lets up wears down sleep, mood, and health.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Stress is a response to pressure.

questions.question: What is a healthy way to manage stress?
questions.correctAnswer: Exercise, sleep, and talking to someone you trust
questions.explanation: Movement burns off stress hormones, sleep resets the brain, and talking shares the load instead of bottling it up.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Move, sleep, and talk.

questions.question: What is depression?
questions.correctAnswer: A mood disorder with lasting sadness and loss of interest
questions.explanation: Unlike ordinary sadness, depression lasts two weeks or more and drains interest even from things a person used to enjoy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Depression lasts and needs help.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend talks about harming themselves?
questions.correctAnswer: Tell a trusted adult right away
questions.explanation: You cannot keep a friend safe alone - telling an adult is not breaking trust, it is getting them protection.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tell an adult right away.

questions.question: What is empathy?
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding and sharing another person's feelings
questions.explanation: Empathy has two parts: noticing what another person feels and imagining the situation from their side.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Empathy is feeling with others.

questions.question: What is peer pressure?
questions.correctAnswer: Pressure from friends to act a certain way
questions.explanation: Peer pressure can be spoken ('just try it') or silent - changing how you act just because the group is doing it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Peers can pressure you.

questions.question: What is a healthy friendship?
questions.correctAnswer: One with respect, trust, and support
distractors: One where one person controls the other
questions.explanation: In a healthy friendship either person can say no, disagree, or be themselves without being punished for it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Healthy friends respect you.

questions.question: What is bullying?
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated hurtful behavior meant to harm someone
questions.explanation: The repetition and the power imbalance are what make it bullying rather than a one-time conflict between equals.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bullying is repeated hurt.

questions.question: What should you do if you are bullied?
questions.correctAnswer: Tell a trusted adult and do not keep it secret
questions.explanation: Reporting is not tattling: adults can only stop bullying they know about, and telling keeps you from facing it alone.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tell an adult about bullying.

questions.question: What is the legal drinking age in the United States?
questions.explanation: The drinking age is 21 in every state - in the 1980s federal funding rules pushed all states to adopt the same minimum.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Drinking age is 21.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to the body?
questions.correctAnswer: It slows the brain and impairs judgment and coordination
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant: even small amounts slow reaction time first, which is what makes it so dangerous for driving.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Alcohol slows the brain.

questions.question: What is the main addictive substance in cigarettes?
questions.correctAnswer: Nicotine
questions.explanation: Nicotine reaches the brain in seconds and rewires its reward system, creating the cravings that make quitting hard.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nicotine is addictive.

questions.question: What is a major health risk of smoking?
questions.correctAnswer: Lung cancer and heart disease
questions.explanation: Tar and carbon monoxide in smoke damage the lungs directly, while nicotine strains the heart and blood vessels.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Smoking harms lungs and heart.

questions.question: What is vaping?
questions.correctAnswer: Inhaling vapor from an electronic cigarette
questions.explanation: An e-cigarette heats a liquid into an aerosol you breathe in - and most of those liquids contain nicotine, so it is not 'just vapor'.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Vaping is not safe.

questions.question: What is a drug?
questions.correctAnswer: A substance that changes how the body or mind works
questions.explanation: Medicines are drugs used to treat illness; the same substance can help or harm depending on the dose and the purpose.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Drugs change the body.

questions.question: What is addiction?
questions.correctAnswer: A strong need to keep using a substance despite harm
questions.explanation: With addiction the brain's reward system is hijacked, so willpower alone is rarely enough - treatment and support help people recover.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Addiction is use despite harm.

questions.question: What is the best way to refuse drugs or alcohol?
questions.correctAnswer: Say no clearly and walk away
distractors: Ignore the offer silently and stay
questions.explanation: A short, clear refusal - 'No thanks, I am good' - plus leaving removes you before the pressure can build.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Say no and walk away.

questions.question: What is the main function of the skeletal system?
questions.correctAnswer: To support the body and protect organs
questions.explanation: The skeleton is also a factory and a storehouse: bones make blood cells and hold minerals such as calcium.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bones support and protect.

questions.question: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.explanation: Babies start with about 300 bones; many fuse together as they grow, leaving 206 separate bones in adults.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Adults have 206 bones.

questions.question: What is the main function of muscles?
questions.correctAnswer: To move the body
questions.explanation: Muscles work by contracting - they can only pull, never push, so they often work in pairs such as the biceps and triceps.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Muscles move you.

questions.question: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.correctAnswer: Skin
questions.explanation: Skin does more than cover you: it blocks germs, holds in fluids, and helps control body temperature.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Skin is the biggest organ.

questions.question: What is the main function of the digestive system?
questions.correctAnswer: To break down food and absorb nutrients
questions.explanation: Digestion is a two-part job: breaking food into pieces small enough to pass into the blood, then absorbing them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Digestion breaks food down.

questions.question: What is the main function of the nervous system?
questions.correctAnswer: To send signals and control the body
questions.explanation: Signals travel as tiny electrical pulses along nerve cells, which is how the brain controls movement and senses the world.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nerves send signals.

questions.question: What is the main function of the kidneys?
questions.correctAnswer: To filter waste from the blood
distractors: To produce red blood cells only
questions.explanation: Each kidney filters about half a cup of blood every minute and turns the waste it removes into urine.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Kidneys filter blood.

questions.question: What is the main function of the liver?
questions.correctAnswer: To filter blood and help digestion
questions.explanation: The liver also makes bile for digestion, stores energy as glycogen, and breaks down alcohol and medicines.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The liver filters blood.

questions.question: What is hygiene?
questions.correctAnswer: Practices that keep the body clean and healthy
questions.explanation: Daily habits such as showering, washing hands, and wearing clean clothes remove the germs and oils that cause illness and odor.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hygiene keeps you clean.

questions.question: Why is brushing teeth important?
questions.correctAnswer: It removes plaque and prevents cavities
questions.explanation: Plaque is a sticky film of bacteria; left in place it hardens into tartar, and its acids eat holes in tooth enamel.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Brush to prevent cavities.

questions.question: How often should you brush your teeth?
questions.correctAnswer: At least twice a day
questions.explanation: Brush morning and night, about two minutes each time, and floss daily to reach the surfaces a brush misses.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Brush twice a day.

questions.question: What is sunscreen for?
questions.correctAnswer: Protecting skin from harmful ultraviolet rays
questions.explanation: Sunscreen absorbs or reflects UV before it can reach skin cells, where it would otherwise damage DNA and raise skin-cancer risk.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sunscreen blocks UV.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe in the sun?
questions.correctAnswer: Wear sunscreen, a hat, and protective clothing
distractors: Stay in the sun all day without protection
questions.explanation: Clothing and shade block UV physically, and avoiding the strongest midday sun, roughly 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., cuts exposure the most.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cover up in the sun.

questions.question: What is a seat belt for?
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping you safe in a car crash
questions.explanation: In a crash your body keeps moving at the car's speed until something stops it; the belt spreads that force across your strongest bones.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wear a seat belt.

questions.question: Why should you not text while driving?
questions.correctAnswer: It distracts you and greatly raises crash risk
questions.explanation: Looking at a phone for five seconds at highway speed means driving the length of a football field without seeing the road.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Never text and drive.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a helmet when biking?
questions.correctAnswer: To protect the head from injury
questions.explanation: A helmet's foam crushes on impact, absorbing energy that would otherwise go straight into the skull and brain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Helmets protect heads.

questions.question: What is a healthy body image?
questions.correctAnswer: Feeling good about your body as it is
questions.explanation: Healthy bodies naturally come in many shapes; a healthy body image judges your body by what it can do, not by photos of models.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Accept your body.

questions.question: What is an eating disorder?
questions.correctAnswer: An unhealthy pattern of eating that harms health
questions.explanation: Anorexia, bulimia, and binge-eating disorder are illnesses, not choices or vanity - they need medical and psychological treatment.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Eating disorders harm health.

questions.question: What is the best snack choice after exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: Water and a snack with protein and carbohydrates
questions.explanation: Exercise empties the muscles' stored fuel and breaks down fibers: carbohydrates refill the fuel and protein supplies the repair material.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Water plus protein and carbs.

questions.question: What is the difference between a food allergy and a food intolerance?
questions.correctAnswer: An allergy involves the immune system; intolerance does not
questions.explanation: In an intolerance, such as lactose intolerance, an enzyme is missing so digestion struggles - uncomfortable, but not life-threatening the way an allergy can be.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Allergy is immune.

questions.question: What should you do if someone has a severe allergic reaction?
questions.correctAnswer: Call 911 and use an epinephrine auto-injector if available
questions.explanation: Epinephrine opens the airways and raises blood pressure during anaphylaxis; it works best when injected into the thigh right away.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Call 911 for severe allergy.

questions.question: What is the Heimlich maneuver for?
questions.correctAnswer: Dislodging food stuck in the airway
questions.explanation: Each upward thrust squeezes the lungs so the burst of air pops the object out, like a cork from a bottle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Heimlich clears airways.

questions.question: What is the first thing to check if someone is unconscious?
questions.correctAnswer: If they are breathing and have a pulse
questions.explanation: Breathing and pulse tell you whether CPR is needed: if neither is normal, call 911 and start chest compressions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Check breathing first.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent cavities?
questions.correctAnswer: Brush, floss, and limit sugary foods
questions.explanation: Floss removes plaque between the teeth, where a brush cannot reach, and less sugar means bacteria make less acid.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Brush and floss.

questions.question: What is the role of a school counselor?
questions.correctAnswer: To help students with school, personal, and career concerns
questions.explanation: Counselors are trained listeners with confidentiality rules, so students can talk about problems without it becoming classroom news.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Counselors help students.

questions.question: What is consent?
questions.correctAnswer: Clear agreement to do something, given freely
questions.explanation: Consent can be withdrawn at any time, and silence, pressure, or a past yes do not count as agreement.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Consent means clear yes.

questions.question: What is a boundary in a relationship?
questions.correctAnswer: A limit that protects your comfort and safety
questions.explanation: A boundary might sound like 'I need my phone back at night' - stating limits early prevents bigger conflicts later.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Boundaries protect you.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a disagreement with a friend?
questions.correctAnswer: Talk calmly and listen to each other
questions.explanation: Using 'I feel...' statements instead of blame keeps a hard conversation from turning into a shouting match.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Talk and listen.

questions.question: What is mindfulness?
questions.correctAnswer: Paying attention to the present moment without judgment
questions.explanation: Simple practice trains it: focus on your breath, and when your mind wanders, gently bring it back without judging yourself.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mindfulness is being present.

questions.question: What is the effect of regular exercise on mood?
questions.correctAnswer: It can improve mood and reduce stress
questions.explanation: Exercise releases endorphins and improves sleep, and both effects feed back into a steadier, better mood.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Exercise lifts mood.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent the flu?
questions.correctAnswer: Get a flu vaccine and wash hands often
questions.explanation: The flu shot is updated every year because flu viruses keep changing; handwashing removes virus your hands pick up from surfaces.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Vaccine and handwashing prevent flu.

questions.question: What is the main function of the excretory system?
questions.correctAnswer: To remove waste from the body
questions.explanation: The kidneys and bladder, the lungs, and the skin all take part: urine, exhaled carbon dioxide, and sweat all carry waste out.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Excretion removes waste.

questions.question: What is a balanced meal?
questions.correctAnswer: A meal with foods from several food groups
questions.explanation: Think of the plate method: half the plate fruits and vegetables, the rest split between grains and protein, with dairy on the side.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Balance means several groups.

questions.question: Why is breakfast important?
questions.correctAnswer: It gives energy after the night fast
questions.explanation: The word breakfast literally means breaking the fast: after 8 to 10 hours without food, blood sugar needs a refill.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Breakfast starts the day.

questions.question: What is the best drink for hydration during exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: Water
questions.explanation: For activity under about an hour, plain water replaces sweat losses best; sports drinks mainly help during long, intense exercise.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Water hydrates best.

questions.question: Besides abstinence, which method greatly reduces the risk of HIV and other STIs during sex?
questions.correctAnswer: Using a condom correctly every time
distractors: Using birth control pills every day
Choosing a partner who looks healthy
questions.explanation: Condoms, used correctly every time, greatly reduce the risk of HIV and many other STIs. Pills prevent pregnancy only, and infections often have no visible signs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Every time, correctly - that is how condoms protect.

questions.question: How is HIV different from AIDS?
questions.correctAnswer: HIV is the virus; AIDS is the advanced stage when the immune system is badly damaged
distractors: They are two completely different viruses
AIDS comes first and turns into HIV
HIV is the stage and AIDS is the virus
questions.explanation: HIV is the virus that attacks the immune system. Without treatment, the damage can progress to AIDS, the most advanced stage. Modern treatment usually prevents that progression.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: HIV is the virus; AIDS is the late stage.

questions.question: Which contraceptive method also protects against sexually transmitted infections?
questions.correctAnswer: The external (male) condom
questions.explanation: The condom is the only contraceptive that also protects against STIs. Pills, IUDs, and implants prevent pregnancy very well but block no infections.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Only the condom guards against both pregnancy and STIs.

questions.question: What should someone do after a possible exposure to an STI?
questions.correctAnswer: Get tested, pause sexual activity until results, and follow the provider's treatment
distractors: Wait a few months to see what happens
Take vitamin supplements and move on
Have sex only with the same partner until it clears up
questions.explanation: After a possible exposure, testing and treatment protect your health and stop spread. Many STIs are curable, and all are manageable when caught early.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Test, pause, treat - in that order.

questions.question: Which statement about STIs is true?
questions.correctAnswer: Many STIs have no symptoms but can still harm health and spread to partners
distractors: Every STI causes obvious symptoms right away
STIs cannot spread unless symptoms are visible
Only people with many partners can get an STI
questions.explanation: Most STIs are silent at first. Without symptoms, infections can still damage the body over time and pass to partners, which is why testing matters.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Silent does not mean safe - most STIs start quiet.

questions.question: A partner says, 'If you really loved me, you would do it.' What is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Coercion - pressure that can never create real consent
distractors: A normal way to show commitment
questions.explanation: Using guilt or pressure to get sexual activity is coercion. Real consent is freely given without pressure, and love is never proven through sex.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'If you loved me' is pressure, not love - and never consent.

questions.question: Why are long-acting methods like IUDs and implants among the most effective contraceptives?
questions.correctAnswer: They work for years without depending on remembering or correct use every time
distractors: They also block sexually transmitted infections
They are the cheapest methods to buy
They can be removed only by surgery
questions.explanation: IUDs and implants remove user error - once placed, they work for years at over 99 percent effectiveness. They do not protect against STIs, so condoms still matter for infection protection.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Set-and-forget methods win because there is nothing to forget.

questions.question: Where can a teen in California get sexual health services confidentially?
questions.correctAnswer: At a clinic - California law lets minors consent to many sexual health services confidentially
distractors: Nowhere - a parent must always be told first
questions.explanation: California law allows minors to consent to many sexual health services, such as STI testing and contraception, without parental notification. Clinics can explain exactly what stays confidential.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: In California, clinics can help teens confidentially.

questions.question: What does 'undetectable = untransmittable' mean for people living with HIV?
questions.correctAnswer: A person whose treatment keeps HIV undetectable does not transmit it sexually
distractors: The virus is cured and gone forever
The person no longer needs any medication
Testing is no longer needed after starting treatment
questions.explanation: HIV treatment can lower the virus to undetectable levels. Studies show a person who stays undetectable does not pass HIV to sexual partners - treatment is also prevention.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Undetectable means untransmittable - treatment protects partners too.

questions.question: Which of these is an early warning sign of dating abuse?
questions.correctAnswer: Extreme jealousy and trying to isolate you from friends and family
distractors: Disagreeing about which movie to watch
Wanting to spend lots of time together
Feeling nervous before a first date
questions.explanation: Isolation is a core abuse tactic: a controlling partner cuts you off from the people who could support you. Extreme jealousy, constant accusations, and monitoring are warning signs to take seriously from the very start.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: jealousy that isolates you is a warning sign.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a healthy dating relationship?
questions.correctAnswer: You can be honest, disagree respectfully, and keep your own friendships
distractors: Your partner decides who you are allowed to talk to
You often feel afraid of your partner's reactions
Your partner reads your messages every day
questions.explanation: In a healthy relationship both partners feel safe being themselves. Disagreements happen without fear, boundaries are respected, and neither person gives up their friends, family, or interests.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: healthy means honest, respectful, and still yourself.

questions.question: An abusive partner constantly puts their partner down, controls the money, and dictates what they wear. These are examples of:
questions.correctAnswer: Power and control - the pattern at the center of dating abuse
distractors: Stress that will pass on its own
Signs the partner just needs more attention
questions.explanation: Dating abuse is not about anger or stress - it is a pattern of behaviors used to hold power and control over a partner: insults, threats, isolation, monitoring, and controlling money, clothes, and activities.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: abuse is a pattern of power and control.

questions.question: Your friend wants to end an abusive relationship but is scared of what their partner might do. What is a helpful response?
questions.correctAnswer: Support their decision, help them think through a safety plan, and connect them with a trusted adult or a hotline
distractors: Tell them to stay until the partner calms down
Break up with the partner on your friend's behalf
Tell them it is partly their fault for staying so long
questions.explanation: Leaving is often the most dangerous time in an abusive relationship, so support and planning matter. Stand by your friend without blame, help them plan how to stay safe, and involve a trusted adult or a dating-abuse hotline.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: support the decision, plan for safety, never blame.

questions.question: Why might a teen stay in an abusive relationship instead of leaving right away?
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of retaliation, threats, isolation, and the manipulated hope that the partner will change
distractors: Because the abuse is not actually serious
Because leaving is always easy and completely safe
questions.explanation: Abusive partners use threats, fear, and isolation to trap their victims, and often mix abuse with apologies and promises to change. That is why victims deserve support, never blame - leaving can be the riskiest step, not the simplest one.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fear traps victims - support frees them.

questions.question: What is human trafficking?
questions.correctAnswer: Exploiting a person through force, fraud, or coercion for labor or commercial sex
distractors: A legal way for teens to earn money quickly
Something that only happens in other countries
Traveling abroad for a new job
questions.explanation: Trafficking means exploiting someone through force, fraud, or coercion - violence and threats (force), lies and false promises (fraud), or pressure and manipulation (coercion). It happens in the United States, in cities and small towns alike - and when a minor is involved in commercial sex, it is trafficking by law even without proof of force or fraud.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: trafficking is exploitation by force, fraud, or coercion.

questions.question: A person online offers you a modeling job that requires travel, keeping it secret from your parents, and sending photos first. This is most likely:
questions.correctAnswer: A trafficking or exploitation recruitment scam
distractors: A normal way first jobs are offered
questions.explanation: Real employers do not demand secrecy from parents or personal photos up front. Travel plus secrecy plus photo requests is a textbook recruitment pattern - end contact, save the messages, and tell a trusted adult.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: secret travel plus photos equals a recruitment scam.

questions.question: Which habit best protects you from online groomers and recruiters?
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping accounts private, never sharing your location or personal details with online-only contacts, and telling an adult about suspicious approaches
distractors: Accepting friend requests from anyone with lots of followers
Using a fake name, which makes everything else safe
Meeting online contacts alone first, to check if they are real
questions.explanation: Privacy settings, guarding personal information and location, and involving a trusted adult early are the strongest defenses. A fake name alone does not protect you, and meeting an online contact alone is exactly what recruiters count on.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: private accounts and a trusted adult shut recruiters out.

questions.question: Which statement about trafficking victims is true?
questions.correctAnswer: Victims can be any gender or background, and many are recruited by someone they know or trust
distractors: Victims are almost always kidnapped by strangers
Only teens who run away can be trafficked
Victims could simply leave whenever they want
questions.explanation: Kidnapping is rare in trafficking. Most victims are manipulated by someone they know - a 'friend,' a romantic partner, sometimes even a family member - and are held by fear, threats, debt, or dependence rather than chains. Anyone can be targeted.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: anyone can be targeted - recruiters are often trusted faces.

questions.question: In sexual abuse prevention, 'grooming' means:
questions.correctAnswer: A pattern where an adult (or older teen) slowly builds trust with a teen and pushes boundaries - special attention, gifts, secrets, and alone time - to make abuse easier and keep it hidden
distractors: Any friendly behavior by a coach or teacher
A normal stage of every mentoring relationship
When two teens in a dating relationship argue often
questions.explanation: Grooming is deliberate: the offender earns trust and lowers defenses step by step - singling the teen out, creating secrets, arranging time alone, and testing physical boundaries - so the abuse can happen and stay hidden.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: trust built in secret steps is a grooming pattern.

questions.question: When a teen discloses sexual abuse, a trusted adult's most important first response is to:
questions.correctAnswer: Believe them, stay calm, and make clear that the abuse is not their fault
distractors: Promise to keep it a complete secret no matter what
Confront the accused person immediately, alone
questions.explanation: Belief and calm support come first. An adult should never promise total secrecy - teachers and many other adults are mandated reporters who must pass the report on so the teen can be protected.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: believe first - it is never the victim's fault.

questions.question: In Illinois, suspected child sexual abuse can be reported by:
questions.correctAnswer: Calling the Illinois DCFS Child Abuse Hotline at 1-800-25-ABUSE (1-800-252-2873), or telling a teacher, counselor, or other trusted adult
distractors: Only filing a report after turning 18
Posting the details on social media
questions.explanation: Illinois runs a statewide child abuse hotline (DCFS, 1-800-25-ABUSE) that anyone can call. Telling a trusted adult at school also works - school staff are mandated reporters who must pass it on the same day.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1-800-25-ABUSE - Illinois's line for reporting abuse.

questions.question: Which pattern is a red flag for grooming by an adult?
questions.correctAnswer: Singling one teen out with gifts and rides, insisting on secrecy, finding reasons to be alone together, and gradually increasing physical contact like 'accidental' touches
distractors: A coach who praises the whole team equally
A teacher who keeps the classroom door open during meetings
A mentor who includes parents in group messages
questions.explanation: Each behavior alone can look innocent; together they form the grooming pattern - special status, secrecy, isolation, and boundary testing. Open doors and parent-inclusive communication are the opposite: protective behavior.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: gifts, secrets, alone time, touches - the pattern is the warning.

questions.question: Teens who are sexually abused often delay telling anyone mainly because of:
questions.correctAnswer: Shame, self-blame, fear of not being believed, and the abuser's manipulation - none of which make the abuse the teen's fault
distractors: A legal rule that reports must wait a year
The abuse usually not being serious enough to mention
questions.explanation: Delayed disclosure is the norm, not the exception. Abusers engineer silence with threats, gifts, and blame-shifting, and teens often fear the reaction as much as the abuser. The responsibility is always the offender's.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: silence is engineered by abusers - blame never belongs to the teen.

questions.question: A friend confides that an adult has been sending them sexual messages. The best response is to:
questions.correctAnswer: Encourage them to tell a trusted adult or report it, offer to go with them, and not forward or share the messages
distractors: Keep it completely secret to protect your friend's privacy
Reply to the adult yourself to scare them off
Ask your friend to send you the messages so you can post them as proof
questions.explanation: Supporting a friend means connecting them to adults who can act - and going along for support. Sharing sexual messages involving a minor spreads harm and can itself be illegal; secrecy protects only the offender.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: walk with your friend to help - never spread the messages.

questions.question: Which statement about child sexual abuse is accurate?
questions.correctAnswer: Most abusers are someone the teen and family know and trust, not strangers
distractors: Most abusers are strangers who approach teens in public places
Abuse only happens in certain kinds of families
A teen's clothing or behavior can make them responsible if it happens
questions.explanation: The large majority of child sexual abuse is committed by a known, trusted person - a relative, family friend, coach, or mentor. That is exactly why grooming works, and why 'stranger danger' alone is not enough protection.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: most abusers are known and trusted - that is the hard truth.

questions.question: An adult asks a teen to keep their private chats and meetings secret from the teen's parents. This is concerning mainly because:
questions.correctAnswer: Secrecy is a core grooming tool - healthy adults do not build hidden relationships with teens; unlike a surprise, which is temporary and meant to be shared, this kind of secret is meant to isolate
distractors: Every secret between any two people is equally dangerous
It proves abuse has already happened in every case
Teens should never keep anything at all private from parents
questions.explanation: The secrets-versus-surprises distinction grows up with students: a surprise party is time-limited and joyful; an adult demanding a hidden relationship is isolating the teen from the people who would protect them - a classic grooming step.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: surprises get shared - isolating secrets are a warning.

questions.question: A coach always texts one teammate privately, gives her rides home alone, and comments on her body. The most accurate reading is:
questions.correctAnswer: These are boundary violations and grooming warning signs that should be reported to a trusted adult or administrator, even if no touching has occurred
distractors: The teammate's private responsibility to handle alone
Typical coaching behavior that should not be questioned
questions.explanation: Grooming is reportable before any contact abuse happens - private messaging, alone time, and body comments from an authority figure are exactly the early pattern Erin's Law teaches students to name and report.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: report the pattern early - you do not wait for worse.

questions.question: Under Virginia law, health instruction in grade 9 or 10 must include research-based instruction on which topic?
questions.correctAnswer: Hazing prevention
questions.explanation: Virginia Code 22.1-207(B), added in 2024, directs that research-based hazing prevention instruction be developed for health and physical education in grade 9 or 10.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Virginia requires hazing prevention instruction in grade 9 or 10 health.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a high school health classroom with a teacher leading a respectful discussion circle of students, a blank presentation board behind them. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Virginia law requires hazing prevention instruction in grade 9 or 10.
img.title: REQUIRED HAZING PREVENTION

questions.question: Which definition of hazing is correct?
questions.correctAnswer: Endangering a student's health or safety, or forcing humiliating or harmful acts, as a condition of joining or staying in a group
distractors: Any practice or workout that feels physically hard
A welcome celebration that new members freely choose and can leave at any time
Friendly teasing between close friends who can stop it at will
questions.explanation: Hazing is conduct that endangers health or safety - or forces degrading acts - tied to initiation into or membership in a team, club, or organization. Hard training and voluntary celebrations are not hazing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hazing endangers or degrades someone to belong to a group.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a concerned student watching a group initiation scene from a doorway, dramatic light emphasizing the danger, no violence shown. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Hazing is endangering or degrading acts tied to joining a group.
img.title: WHAT HAZING MEANS

questions.question: A senior says a new teammate 'agreed to it, so it is not hazing.' Why is that reasoning wrong?
questions.correctAnswer: Hazing is unlawful even when the person says they consent - agreement does not make endangering initiation acts legal or safe
distractors: It is wrong only because the senior is not the team captain
Consent always cancels any school rule about group activities
New members can consent, but only in writing and with a coach present
questions.explanation: Under Virginia's hazing law, the victim's apparent consent is not a defense: initiation acts that endanger health or safety are prohibited whether or not the person went along with them, often under heavy peer pressure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Saying yes under pressure does not make hazing legal.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a young athlete looking pressured and isolated while older teammates stand around in a locker room corridor, tense atmosphere, no violence shown. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Consent is not a defense to hazing under Virginia law.
img.title: CONSENT IS NO EXCUSE FOR HAZING

questions.question: Forcing a new member to drink large amounts of alcohol quickly is especially dangerous because:
questions.correctAnswer: Rapid drinking can cause alcohol poisoning, which can stop breathing and kill - and hazers often delay calling for help
distractors: It is only risky if the person has never tasted alcohol before
The main danger is embarrassment the next day at school
Large amounts are safe if the group stays indoors together
questions.explanation: Forced rapid drinking is one of the deadliest hazing patterns: blood alcohol can keep rising after the person passes out, suppressing breathing, and fear of punishment often delays the 911 call that could save them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Forced drinking can kill - and fear delays the rescue call.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of an unconscious young person at a party being helped by a worried friend reaching for a phone to call emergency services, bottles pushed aside. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Forced drinking risks fatal alcohol poisoning; call for help immediately.
img.title: DEADLY DRINKING HAZING

questions.question: You learn that teammates plan to haze new players next weekend. What is the most protective action?
questions.correctAnswer: Tell a trusted adult, coach, or administrator now - reporting before it happens can prevent the harm entirely
distractors: Stay silent so you are not seen as disloyal to the team
Warn only the new players and let them handle it alone
Film the event so there is evidence afterward
questions.explanation: Bystander reporting is a core hazing-prevention skill: telling a trusted adult or administrator, or using a school reporting channel, can stop a planned event before anyone is hurt.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Report a planned hazing before it happens - silence protects the hazing, not the team.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a student speaking privately and seriously with a school counselor in an office, relieved expression. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Report planned hazing to a trusted adult before it happens.
img.title: SPEAK UP BEFORE IT HAPPENS

questions.question: Virginia family life standards require prevention teaching on sexual harassment 'using electronic means.' Which behavior fits that phrase?
questions.correctAnswer: Repeatedly sending unwanted sexual messages or images, or pressuring someone by phone or social media for sexual photos
distractors: Sending a friend a homework reminder by text
Following a classmate's public sports account
Losing an online game and sending a frustrated message
questions.explanation: Sexual harassment using electronic means is harassment carried out through technology: unwanted sexual texts or images, repeated sexual comments online, or pressuring someone for intimate photos.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Electronic sexual harassment is unwanted sexual messages, images, or pressure online.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a student looking distressed at a phone glowing with generic blurred message bubbles, a supportive friend beside them. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Unwanted sexual messages or photo pressure online is electronic sexual harassment.
img.title: HARASSMENT THROUGH A SCREEN

questions.question: Someone shares a classmate's private intimate photo in a group chat without that person's permission. The best description is:
questions.correctAnswer: Sexual harassment and a serious violation - the sharing itself is the harm, and it should be reported, not forwarded
distractors: A harmless joke as long as the sharer did not take the photo
Acceptable if the two students used to date
Only a problem if a teacher happens to see it
questions.explanation: Sharing an intimate image without consent is a form of sexual harassment and abuse: each forward spreads the harm. The protective response is to not forward it, support the person targeted, and report it to a trusted adult or the platform.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Never forward an intimate image - report it and support the person.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a student firmly turning a phone face down while friends look on seriously, a teacher approaching supportively in a school hallway. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Sharing an intimate image without consent is sexual harassment - do not forward it.
img.title: NEVER FORWARD IT

questions.question: Which statement about consent matches what Virginia instruction must teach about its law and meaning?
questions.correctAnswer: Consent must be freely given by a person who is able to decide - it cannot be obtained by pressure, and a person who is incapacitated by alcohol or drugs cannot consent
distractors: Consent is assumed unless the person physically resists
Once someone agrees to one activity, they have agreed to everything
Silence or going along out of fear counts as consent
questions.explanation: Virginia family life instruction covers the law and meaning of consent: agreement must be free and informed, pressure or force voids it, and someone who is incapacitated cannot legally consent.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Real consent is free, informed, and from someone able to decide.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of two students in a calm respectful conversation in a school common area, body language showing listening and clear communication. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Consent must be freely given by someone able to decide.
img.title: THE MEANING OF CONSENT
